text: Soil_1_10 is a biosynthetic gene cluster identified solely by DeepBGC, with no compound class assigned.
It spans 49 kb on contig_1 from position 936,108 to 985,530 and contains 46 genes.

No comparison with MIBiG has been made, as antiSMASH did not detect this locus.

The presence of xanthine dehydrogenase subunits and accessory factors, along with oxidoreductases and transcriptional regulators, suggests the cluster may be involved in purine degradation rather than specialised metabolite production.

Soil_1_13 is a nonribosomal peptide (NRPS) cluster detected by antiSMASH, DeepBGC and GECCO, spanning 57 kb on contig_1 and containing 30 genes.
antiSMASH marks 11 genes as biosynthetic, comprising 2 core and 9 additional genes, with 4 regulatory and 3 transport genes also present.

CJLEIP_01147, a D-alanine--poly(phosphoribitol) ligase subunit DltA, contains 3 modules with adenylation domains predicted to load phenylalanine, an unidentified residue and valine, and one module carries an epimerization domain.

CJLEIP_01149, also a D-alanine--poly(phosphoribitol) ligase subunit DltA, has 3 modules with adenylation domains predicted to load an unidentified residue, threonine and threonine, and two modules carry an epimerization domain.

Together CJLEIP_01147 and CJLEIP_01149 hold 6 modules; antiSMASH predicts substrates for 4 modules (phenylalanine, valine and two threonine) and none for 2 modules, with 3 modules carrying an epimerization domain.
CJLEIP_01154, annotated as a Thioesterase, is named a core gene by DeepBGC and GECCO.

Additional biosynthetic genes include CJLEIP_01139 (Glycosyltransferase family 1 protein), CJLEIP_01148 (MbtH family protein), CJLEIP_01152 (Cytochrome P450) and CJLEIP_01161 (23S rRNA methyltransferase RlmD).
The closest known cluster is BGC0002358 (cyclofaulknamycin) from Streptomyces albidoflavus, which is a close match.

CJLEIP_01147 matches XNR_0983 (Peptide synthase) of BGC0002358 at 99 % identity, CJLEIP_01149 matches XNR_0985 (Peptide synthase) at 99 % identity, and CJLEIP_01154 matches XNR_0990 (putative thioesterase) at 99 % identity.

The cluster may produce a modified nonribosomal peptide, possibly incorporating phenylalanine, valine and threonine, based on the core NRPS genes and tailoring enzymes such as cytochrome P450 and glycosyltransferase, while the presence of regulatory and transport genes suggests specialised metabolite biosynthesis rather than primary metabolism.
Soil_1_15 is a terpene biosynthetic gene cluster detected by antiSMASH, DeepBGC and GECCO, spanning 21 kb on contig_1 and containing 22 genes.
antiSMASH marks 4 genes as biosynthetic, comprising 1 core gene and 3 additional biosynthetic genes, with 2 regulatory and 1 transport gene also present.
The core gene CJLEIP_01467 is annotated as a terpene synthase by Bakta and identified as such by antiSMASH and GECCO.

Together, the additional biosynthetic genes include CJLEIP_01462 (short chain dehydrogenase), CJLEIP_01469 (citramalate synthase), and CJLEIP_01472 (urease subunit alpha), each marked by antiSMASH as biosynthetic.
The closest known cluster is BGC0001181 (geosmin) from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2), a terpene cluster with questionable annotation quality in MIBiG.

One gene in the locus, CJLEIP_01467, matches the putative cyclase CAB41566.1 in BGC0001181 at 64% identity, and antiSMASH finds counterparts for 100% of that cluster's genes, indicating a moderate match overall.

The cluster may produce a terpene-based metabolite, possibly related to geosmin, given the presence of a terpene synthase core gene and additional modifying enzymes such as a short chain dehydrogenase and citramalate synthase, alongside urease components that could influence nitrogen metabolism or precursor availability.
